clue.text: Parker's transgression clamped down on by law?

definitions.text: Parker's transgression clamped down on by law?

parts.words: Parker's transgression clamped down on by law?
parts.note: a driver who parks illegally may have a wheel clamp, known as a Denver boot, fitted by the authorities, and the phrase for being dismissed reads literally

explanation.surface: A motorist's parking offence is dealt with firmly by the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means sacked; here it is read literally, the wheel clamp being nicknamed a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A car fitted with a wheel clamp has literally received a boot, while the idiom means dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Be a girl for a change, there's an angel!

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters of 'Be a girl' produces a new word

explanation.surface: Someone acting as a girl for once is called heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who brings messages in the Bible.

clue.text: Drapery able to be replaced in a depression

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

indicators.note: the letters of the word for able are put back in a different order

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, so able means can

explanation.surface: Curtain material that can be swapped out sits in a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN (able) is rearranged by 'to be replaced' to ANC, which goes 'in' VALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a short curtain or frill of fabric hung round a bed or window, a kind of drapery.

clue.text: Almost your lot, so to speak (6, 3) 460 minutes one spent with an attractive female

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held runs two clues together by OCR ('Almost your lot, so to speak (6, 3) 460 minutes one spent with an attractive female (9)'), and the wordplay of 'your lot, so to speak' for the answer is unclear with no scan to confirm the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Almost your lot, so to speak (6, 3) 460 minutes one spent with an attractive female

clue.text: 60 minutes one spent with an attractive female

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An hour of someone's time is spent in the company of a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of paradise in Islamic tradition, hence any alluring woman.

clue.text: See Cuba differently for that reason

indicators.note: arranging the letters another way gives a new word

explanation.surface: An invitation to view Cuba in a new light, with a reason given.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces a cause, meaning on the grounds that.

clue.text: It's the Pacific I associate with a group of islands

parts.note: the Pacific is the largest ocean
A is an abbreviation for associate, as in a professional title

explanation.surface: A traveller links the Pacific to a cluster of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the name for the islands of the central and south Pacific, taken together as a region.

clue.text: Lively members of the ETU?

parts.note: the ETU was the Electrical Trades Union, whose members are electricians, nicknamed sparks, and lively means bright

explanation.surface: Energetic trade unionists in the electrical industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The ETU was the British Electrical Trades Union; electricians are informally called sparks, and the phrase also means clever people.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever, quick-witted people are called this, and electricians who are keen would literally be bright electrical workers.

clue.text: To stroke a girl is rash

parts.note: to stroke is to rub gently
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Stroking a young woman is reckless behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like the adjective meaning reckless; it is the noun, a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is a mild illness marked by a red skin eruption.

clue.text: Not obvious a relative has a right

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation

explanation.surface: It is far from clear that a relation is in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazy or ambiguous is not easy to see or understand.

clue.text: Concerning payment for moving house, perhaps

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a settlement is the paying of a bill

explanation.surface: A query about the bill for a removal firm's services.
explanation.definitionFit: Relocating to a new home is an example of moving to live somewhere else, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: French puppet grand in a horror play

definitions.meaning: the traditional glove-puppet character of Lyon, the French counterpart of Punch
the Grand ___ was a Paris theatre of gruesome plays, and its name now labels any horror drama

explanation.surface: A Paris marionette plays a big part in a frightening drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyon puppet gave its name to the Paris theatre whose gory shows made 'Grand ___' a byword for macabre entertainment.

clue.text: Lizards using a double disguise

indicators.note: the letters are disguised by being put in a new order
the single letter a is taken twice over

explanation.surface: Reptiles take on a twofold camouflage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' makes AA from 'a'; with USING that is rearranged by 'disguise'.
explanation.definitionFit: These large tropical American reptiles are a family of lizards.

clue.text: Fine fabric placed in a French department

definitions.meaning: a soft, fine silk or nylon net used for veils
a town that is the chief town of the Corrèze department in central France

explanation.surface: Delicate material set down in a Paris shop's section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'department' suggests a store section, but it is a French administrative region.
explanation.definitionFit: The netting took its name from the town in Corrèze where it was first made.

clue.text: Vehicle of a G.B S. play liable to upset

definitions.text: Vehicle of a G.B S. play liable to upset

parts.words: Vehicle of a G.B S. play liable to upset
parts.note: George Bernard Shaw wrote a play named after a fruit seller's barrow, and the idiom about upsetting plans names the same barrow

explanation.surface: A conveyance in a Shaw drama is prone to being knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: G.B.S. is George Bernard Shaw; to upset the ___ is to spoil a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow for fruit is the vehicle in the title of Shaw's 1929 play and in the idiom for wrecking plans.

clue.text: Unprofitable outcome of a trawl

parts.note: a fishing trip that brings in few fish is a disappointing haul

explanation.surface: A fishing boat returns with a disappointing haul.
explanation.definitionFit: A meagre haul of fish is a bad result for a trawler, and the phrase also suits an unsuitable partner.

clue.text: A case for the papers

parts.note: a flat carrying case for documents, and also the office of a minister, whose papers concern a department

explanation.surface: A story fit for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests the press and 'case' a news story; it is a document holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat leather folder holds loose sheets of documents or drawings.

clue.text: Music finding 20 out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the number points to the answer at 20 down, a fictional French detective

explanation.surface: Discovering tunes after twenty goes awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of the 20-down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Syncopated piano style of the early 1900s, as played by Scott Joplin, is a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Mineral self-correcting on average

indicators.note: correcting the word self puts its letters right in a new order

parts.note: par is the average or normal level

explanation.surface: A rock that puts itself right, on average.
explanation.definitionFit: Felspar, or feldspar, is a group of rock-forming silicate minerals common in granite.

clue.text: Animal arrived late

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, meaning arrived
L is an abbreviation for late

explanation.surface: A creature turned up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The humped desert beast of burden is a large mammal.

clue.text: Rebel Jack went to New Zealand to find a part of a notable movement

parts.note: Jack Cade led a revolt in England in 1450

explanation.surface: An English rebel emigrates to New Zealand to join a famous campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is musical, and 'notable' hints at musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate solo passage near the end of a concerto movement is played by the soloist.

clue.text: Novel detective encountered around troubled Riga

indicators.note: the first word's letters go round the others

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, meaning encountered

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fictional sleuth is found near a strife-torn Latvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges RIGA to AIGR, and 'around' puts MET outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon's Paris police inspector is a detective from crime fiction.

clue.text: Talks about blow-outs?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
gales are strong winds, things that blow hard

explanation.surface: Discussions concerning lavish feasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A blow-out is also a big meal, and to treat guests to one is the answer's other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain listeners with lengthy anecdotes is to hold forth, a sense of speaking at length.

clue.text: Trust misplaced in one giving support

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong places, a new order

explanation.surface: Confidence is wasted on someone who backs you.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace or prop in a framework holds a structure up.

clue.text: Metal of initial concern these days I keep quiet about

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

indicators.note: the word for silence goes round the other letter

parts.note: to keep mum is to say nothing

explanation.surface: A metal causing early worry nowadays, and someone keeps quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft bluish-white element, used in batteries, is a chemical metal.

clue.text: Lamb's position in the team?

parts.note: a young sheep frolics and jumps, and the leader of a side is its captain

explanation.surface: Which role a player named Lamb takes in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambs skip, so one would be a natural leaper; the word also means a team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of a team is so called, and a lamb leaping about in a field literally skips.

clue.text: Look after little Ronald, the young shoot

parts.note: to tend is to look after
Ron is a short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: Care for little Ronald, the youngster growing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendron is a tender new sprout or bud on a plant.

clue.text: Kind of discussion calling for a brew of rather hot tea

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture, so these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A frank chat needs a pot of hot tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid, intimate conversation between two people is so described.
